Replay

Dockyard Duo

6 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Run a prepared candidatePlayBuild from sourceCreate an itch.io ZIP or upload with ButlerCode and evidence

Two salvage robots haul awkward cargo onto an escape barge. Odin owns the game rules, Replay owns prediction/recovery, Box3D owns physics, and Godot owns editor authoring and presentation.

Unreleased review candidate. Actual native/browser multiplayer, full state, recovery, rendered play and audio work in the recorded local cases. Both final 610-second browser arrangements meet the original normal-frame limits. Firefox had one 45.92 ms eight-step correction against a 25 ms maximum; qualification remains rejected. The public Room service is deployed and passed relay/recovery checks from the reference network. Independent off-network acceptance and two-human co-op feedback remain open. See the current build status and handoff. The newer invite usability update adds short room codes and browser-native copy/paste. Its two-player and native checks pass; the public spectator terminal audit remains unresolved. The earlier performance measurements have not been rebound to this newer artifact.

Run a prepared candidate#

Use Godot 4.7.1. The included Native SDK project is macOS ARM64, requiring at least macOS 14.0. It is not a signed app or universal SDK. From the candidate directory, open separate terminals:

Shell
python3 native-macos-arm64/launch.py host --project native-macos-arm64 --godot /PATH/TO/GODOT
python3 native-macos-arm64/launch.py client --project native-macos-arm64 --godot /PATH/TO/GODOT

practice opens one mint-robot window. A compatible native client on another machine can use --address HOST_LAN_IP; both roles use port49791 by default, changed with --port. Native/Web crossplay remains unqualified.

For browser files, run python3 serve-web.py --port 8080 from the candidate. Open the served page with a compatible room service:

Text
http://127.0.0.1:8080/index.html?service=ENCODED_COMPATIBLE_WSS_URL&relay=1

The local file server supplies the required isolation headers. A room service and TURN relay are separate processes; the package includes operator templates and no credentials. Public hosting requires HTTPS/WSS, those headers and actual remote connectivity checks. See deployment configuration. The deployed review Room endpoint is wss://mc.laserturtle.net:62127/replay-room/dockyard; use relay=1 for its authenticated TURN provider. The package README includes the encoded launch URL. Choose a name and Host or Join, sharing the five-character room code. The host's copy button displays the code so a crewmate can also type it directly. On Web, clicking the code field opens a native browser text field: paste with Cmd/Ctrl+V and choose Use code, then Join. The copy dialog uses a native Copy code button and also supports Cmd/Ctrl+C. This works inside itch's iframe without clipboard-read permission. Older complete invitation tickets are still accepted. Separate browser profiles have separate stored identities. Recent Crew reuses membership. Watch uses the same short code to enroll a receive-only observer through its separate invitation.

Play#

Input Action
WASD / arrows Drive relative to the camera
Aim and hold left mouse Pull eligible cargo within reach
Space Acknowledged boost action with cooldown
1 / 2 / 3 Select a load for aim height; hold to aim directly at it
F2 Local sound, camera distance and reduced-effects settings
Escape Crew / leave menu while the shared job continues
F3 Actual session diagnostics

Mint is player1; coral is player2. Pull together up the ramp and match each load to its bay. Release the magnet and allow two seconds to latch. The long load benefits from both players. Robots recover after a fall; lost cargo reduces the payout. Jobs have a150-second deadline, three loads and payouts. At results the host can retry or select the next of three arrangements through a Replay action.

Host loss or expired hosting permission ends the job and offers Start a New Crew after closing the old runtime. Seamless takeover and full-match replay are outside this candidate. See recovery evidence.

Build from source#

Enter nix develop at the repository root and use new cache/output directories. The backend pins Box3D 33626332 from2026-10-28. The driver verifies the complete source/archive and the small shim adaptation.

Shell
bash build/build_box3d.sh Release /tmp/dockyard-native
python3 examples/replay_dockyard/prepare.py \
  --out /tmp/dockyard-build \
  --native-library /tmp/dockyard-native/build/Release/libogb3.dylib \
  --sqlite-library "$(pkg-config --variable=libdir sqlite3)/libsqlite3.a" --build
python3 examples/replay_dockyard/launch.py host --project /tmp/dockyard-build/project
python3 examples/replay_dockyard/launch.py client --project /tmp/dockyard-build/project

The static SQLite input preserves strict Native dependency admission. REPLAY_SQLITE_LIBRARY supplies the same option. Browsers use IndexedDB. Other native targets need their own backend builds and runtime checks; the candidate relocation proof covers macOS ARM64.

For Web, build the SIMD archive and use its printed absolute path:

Shell
bash build/build_box3d.sh WebSIMD /tmp/dockyard-web
python3 build/web_rtc_template.py derive \
  --source "$HOME/Library/Application Support/Godot/export_templates/4.7.1.stable/web_dlink_release.zip" \
  --out /tmp/dockyard-rtc-template
REPLAY_SQLITE_LIBRARY="$(pkg-config --variable=libdir sqlite3)/libsqlite3.a" \
BINARYEN_CORES=1 python3 -B tests/box3d_web/replay/export.py \
  --out /tmp/dockyard-export \
  --native-library /tmp/dockyard-native/build/Release/libogb3.dylib \
  --web-archive /ABSOLUTE/PRINTED/PATH/libogb3.a \
  --odin "$(command -v odin)" --godot "$GODOT" --emcc "$(command -v emcc)" \
  --web-template-record /tmp/dockyard-rtc-template/template-record.json

This uses the normal SDK/import/Godot exporter. BINARYEN_CORES=1 is the controlled optimizer setting used after a retained parallel optimizer crash. It changes no simulation worker, assertion or floating-point policy. The browser checks exercise separate actual clients. Serve one identical artifact to the browser cohort; native/Web crossplay remains unqualified. The pinned custom template changes only the RTC send-copy function in Godot's JavaScript. Its record and reproduction helper accompany the review package; both official engine Wasm payloads stay byte-identical.

After checking those exact runtime bytes, create a review package. The runtime record supplies the compatible room cohort:

Shell
python3 examples/replay_dockyard/package.py collect \
  --export-record /ABSOLUTE/EXPORT/report.json \
  --runtime-report /ABSOLUTE/RUNTIME/report.json \
  --qualification-report tests/replay_dockyard/online/current-handoff-status.json \
  --include-native-sdk --out /tmp/dockyard-candidate
python3 examples/replay_dockyard/package.py verify --package /tmp/dockyard-candidate

Packaging starts no compiler, game or external deployment. It verifies ordinary export bytes, fills the operator cohort from the matching runtime, and retains qualification rejection. It excludes fixture bridges, profiles, private databases, credentials and private keys. Editing the frozen Native project needs the source SDK/tools and a fresh build.

To include Godot's compiled license notices, extract them from the installed engine with engine_notices.gd and pass that output directory as --godot-notices to collect. The extractor records its actual engine version; compiled module inventories can vary by target.

Create an itch.io ZIP or upload with Butler#

From the repository root, point the publishing script at a prepared candidate (the directory containing manifest.json, web/ and qa/, or its review .tar.gz archive):

Shell
bash examples/replay_dockyard/publish.sh --package /PATH/TO/dockyard-candidate
# Or: --package /PATH/TO/Dockyard-Duo-review-public-room-macos-arm64-web.tar.gz

The command prints the ZIP path under examples/replay_dockyard/out/itch-BUILD_ID/. It puts index.html at the archive root, includes the licenses and QA status, and configures the deployed Room endpoint from the candidate's QA record with authenticated TURN enabled. Players can launch without adding URL parameters. --service-url wss://HOST/PATH selects another compatible deployment. The script changes the copied HTML launch defaults; engine JavaScript, Wasm and game PCK bytes retain their candidate hashes. The original candidate is preserved. An identical repeat verifies and reuses the output. --out /NEW/DIRECTORY selects another location. This packages an existing build; source changes require a fresh export and candidate through the commands above.

Upload the printed ZIP on an itch.io HTML project, mark it playable in the browser, and enable SharedArrayBuffer support in its embed settings. Choose a 1280×720 viewport or fullscreen launch. See the itch.io HTML5 upload guide. For a local preview, serve the printed web/ directory with isolation headers:

Shell
bash build/serve.sh /PATH/TO/itch-BUILD_ID/web 8080
# Open http://127.0.0.1:8080/

For an upload workflow similar to Scrapyard's standalone publish.sh, log in once and add an explicit destination:

Shell
nix run nixpkgs#butler -- login
bash examples/replay_dockyard/publish.sh \
  --package /PATH/TO/dockyard-candidate --push YOUR_ACCOUNT/YOUR_GAME

The script uses Butler on PATH, falling back to nix run nixpkgs#butler, and uploads the same unpacked ZIP contents to html5. --channel and --version override those defaults. The upload does not create the itch project or configure its embed options; set those once on the edit page. See the Butler upload guide. The existing open qualification and playtest gates stay recorded in the ZIP.

Code and evidence#

The scene has19 bodies/shapes, eight geometries and one hinge, within the35-body/ shape, one-joint and64MiB admission profile. Magnets use Native ray hits, point impulses and damping. Godot meshes/effects add no physics bodies. Loading draws visual variants before enrollment; tethers/confetti share one opaque material style. Web voices use stream playback through suspend/resume. Confirmed Cue_Route changes drive a bounded sound/effect FIFO once.

The checked flat C body-type addition preserves ABI1/POD layouts and requires current rebuilt libraries. Kit and Replay share the reusable backend. See the contributor tour, round checks, presentation checks, qualification and packaging checks. Earlier reports retain their original build/hardware scopes. Automation, screenshots and nonzero audio signal do not supply human co-op feedback.
